newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African Q3 refined oil products sales up 6.4 pct.
newsitem.headline: S.African Q3 refined oil products sales up 6.4 pct.

text.p: Oil products sales in South Africa grew by 6.4 percent in the third quarter of this year compared to the same quarter in 1995, the South African Petroleum Industry Association said on Wednesday.
"This is the third consecutive quarter of this year in which growth over the corresponding quarter of 1995 has exceeded six percent," it said in a statement.
"This is inspite of significant increases in prices due to higher world oil prices and the weaker rand... and hopefully reflects underlying strength in the South African economy."
The impact of the price increases for gasoline alone was, however, reflected in the fact that sales grew by only 2.8 percent compared to four percent in the second quarter.

Gasoline sales grew to 2.6 billion litres from 2.5 billion litres, diesel by 7.7 percent to 1.5 billion litres from 1.4 billion litres, jet fuel by 21.3 percent to 393 million litres from 324 million litres and paraffin for lighting by 13.5 percent to 261 million litres from 230 million litres.
Fuel oil grew by 20.6 percent to 187 million litres from 155 million litres and bitumen by 3.2 percent to 64 million litres from 62 million litres.
Liquified petroleum gas (LPG) sales fell by 1.6 percent to 121 million litres from 123 million litres.
The penetration of unleaded petrol as a percentage of total sales was 9.2 percent in September.
